newsitem.title: USA: FLEET TO BUY COLUMBIA FUNDS - SOURCE.
newsitem.headline: FLEET TO BUY COLUMBIA FUNDS - SOURCE.

text.p: Fleet Financial Group is close to an agreement to buy Portland, Ore.-based mutual fund company Columbia Management for $400 million in cash plus incentives, a source familiar with the deal told Reuters.
"We don't have an agreement at this point, but we are close to an agreement," the source said.

The agreement calls for Fleet to pay $400 million in cash plus five-year payments to keep Columbia's senior management in place, as well as performance incentives, he said. "For the senior management of Columbia to remain in place, there are payments to be made over a five-year period," he said.

Columbia, which has $22 billion in assets under management, would be operated as an independent business unit under the Columbia name with the same management team, the source said. "The transaction will be accretive to Fleet's earnings from Day One," he said.

The acquisition, expected to be completed any day, would help grow Fleet Investment Advisors, which currently has $52 billion in assets under management. Fleet's goal is to double that amount, the source said.
Mutual fund analysts said Columbia has a good reputation as a small boutique of well-managed funds.
"They are the kind of good, small fund family that is desirable today," Morningstar analyst Bill Rocco told Reuters in an interview.
Columbia runs 12 no-load, growth-oriented funds which total more than $5 billion in assets. The company also manages about $17 billion in private and institutional funds.
The Fleet acquisition is just the latest in a recent spate of bank takeovers of mutual fund companies.

Last month, J.P. Morgan & Co Inc agreed to pay $900 million for a 45 percent stake in Kansas City-based American Century Cos, the 10th largest fund company in the United States in terms of assets under management.
In June, Zurich Group announced it would buy a 69.5 percent stake in Scudder, Stevens & Clark, based in New York, in a deal valued at more than $2 billion.
